subject: Magnus-7b: elevated timeout wave — customer briefing & postmortem
messages:
From: ops-alerts@redwood.ai
To: rafael.mendes@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 27 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: [Alert] Magnus-7b elevated 504/timeouts observed (region: us-west-2)

Team —

We started seeing an uptick in 504/timeouts from the Magnus-7b inference fleet at ~08:55 PDT. Initial scope: roughly 7% of in-flight requests to model "Magnus-7b-v1" returned 504 or timed out between 08:55 and 09:05. Top affected customers (by request volume): Cartograph Analytics, PureMetrics, and two smaller PLG accounts.

Immediate actions taken:
- Automated routing fallback enabled to Magnus-7b-quant and Magnus-6b-compat for requests that matched the latency SLO policy.
- Scaled the dedicated worker pool in us-west-2 by +30% (manual override).
- Throttling rule tightened for long-running streaming sessions created by certain batched workflows.

Impact: Intermittent timeouts and a small increase in 504s for requests with long context windows (> 1,024 tokens). No data plane integrity issues observed; logs show elevated kernel queue latencies and a correlated spike in host GPU memory pressure on nodes running mixed-ctx workloads.

Next: ops will continue rolling affected nodes out of rotation and push a telemetry fix to improve preemption handling. Filing an incident ticket: MAGNUS-20280327. I've attached the short error window logs for triage.

—ops-alerts
(attachment: magnus7b_error_window_logs.zip)

From: Sara O'Neill <sara@cartograph.io>
To: rafael.mendes@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 27 Mar 2028 09:35:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Magnus-7b elevated 504/timeouts observed (region: us-west-2)

Rafael —

Thanks for the heads up. We started seeing a spike in failures in our anomaly detection pipeline around 09:00; across ~60% of our envs the inference call returned a 504 and retried. This inflated our downstream queue and caused a delayed windowing job. Can you confirm whether retries were routed to the quant variant? We rely on consistent logits ordering — switching to quant can change output distributions and would affect a couple of our production validators.

Also, we have a quarterly report due Friday and this failure bumped our SLA error budget. Please keep us posted on mitigation and if Redwood can offer credit for the impacted window.

—Sara
Director, Platform Engineering
Cartograph Analytics

From: rafael.mendes@redwood.ai
To: Sara O'Neill <sara@cartograph.io>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 27 Mar 2028 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Magnus-7b elevated 504/timeouts observed (region: us-west-2)

Sara —

Apologies for the disruption and thank you for the quick note. Short answers first: (1) We attempted to route a portion of traffic to Magnus-7b-quant as an emergency fallback for latency SLOs; that routing was limited and policy-driven (only non-streaming requests that matched fallback fingerprint). We did not automatically re-emit responses to your pipeline.

(2) We are preparing a customer-facing incident summary and a post-incident remediation plan. I want to be explicit on compensatory steps: I'm escalating to request a credit for the affected window and will track this with our billing team. Ben, can you confirm the guideline here for a single short outage affecting multiple calls (we may propose a pro-rata credit tied to the error window)?

Technical context: Ops found that a rare memory compaction pathway (triggered by mixed-length contexts with pinned KV caches) increased scheduler latency and caused delayed accept loops on a subset of worker hosts. Root mitigations we pushed at 09:20: a scheduler timeout patch and temporary isolation of mixed-ctx jobs to a separate worker pool. We observed error rate return to baseline (<=0.5%) by ~09:40 after mitigations.

I'll share a short postmortem within 24 hours that includes causal write-up and longer-term fixes (improved kernel backpressure handling, stricter autoscaling for mixed-ctx work, and extra telemetry for KV cache pressure).

Marissa — please attach the postmortem draft and sign-off items once ready.

Sara — can we schedule a 15-minute call this afternoon if you want to review the postmortem live? I can loop in the ops engineer who led the rollout.

—Rafael
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0182

(attachment: postmortem_draft_v1.pdf)

From: ben.carter@redwood.ai
To: rafael.mendes@redwood.ai, Sara O'Neill <sara@cartograph.io>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 28 Mar 2028 15:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Magnus-7b: elevated timeout wave — customer briefing & postmortem

Sara — Rafael —

Thanks for the patience while we pulled together the closure notes. Attached is the final postmortem and our remediation commitments. Short summary for billing: we will apply a 15% pro-rata credit for the 45-minute impact window (08:55–09:40 PDT) to Cartograph's usage invoice for March. We evaluated the traffic profile and this covers the observed retries and increased queueing costs. If you'd prefer an alternate remedy (e.g., SLA credit + engineering office hours), we can accommodate — let me know.

Operational commitments included in the attached PDF:
- Kernel scheduling hotfix deployed (permanent) — reduces queue latency for mixed-ctx by ~90% in our internal tests.
- Mixed-ctx workload isolation by default for Magnus variants in us-west-2 (configuration rollout this week).
- Additional telemetry for KV cache occupancy and a dashboard we will share with customers for near-real-time visibility.
- Contingency routing rules reviewed and tightened to avoid silent qualitative shifts to quant variants without explicit customer opt-in.

Sara: if you'd like the ops engineer (Amir) to walk through logs with your team, we can set that up.

—Ben
Sr. Customer Reliability Manager, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai
